vi.R: Cô ta cứ đi theo Phao-lô và chúng tôi và kêu lớn: "Những người này là đầy tớ của Đức Chúa Trời Chí Cao! Họ đang cho các người biết làm thế nào để được cứu!"

ko.L: 이 여자가 바울과 우리를 따라다니면서 소리를 질러 말했다. "이 사람들은 가장 높으신 하나님의 종들이다. 너희에게 구원의 길을 선포하고 있다."
ko.B: 그 여자는 바울과 우리를 따라다니면서 외쳤다. "이 사람들은 가장 높으신 하나님의 종들이다! 너희에게 구원의 길을 전하고 있다!"
ko.R: 그 여자는 바울과 우리를 계속 따라다니면서 소리쳤다. "이 사람들은 가장 높으신 하나님의 종들이다! 너희가 어떻게 구원받을 수 있는지 알려 주고 있다!"

decisions.choice: the Most High God: true in itself, but a title pagans also used for their highest god
decisions.reason: The title goes back to Genesis 14:18-20. Demons cried out to Jesus as "Son of the Most High God" (Luke 8:28). In the Greek world, inscriptions honor Zeus and other gods as "the Most High", so hearers in Philippi might not have known which god was meant.

decisions.choice: a way of salvation: one way among others, as her hearers would take it
decisions.reason: There is no article. Her words are true as far as they go, but in a city of many gods they could sound like one more path. This may be why Paul was troubled (16:18).

decisions.choice: slaves: men wholly owned by God
decisions.reason: The word means a slave. The apostles use it of themselves (Romans 1:1; Philippians 1:1) and of believers in prayer (4:29).

decisions.choice: these men: Paul and his companions
decisions.reason: The word here points to particular men, the missionaries.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "to you"
decisions.reason: The two Greek pronouns sounded alike and were often confused by copyists. "To you" is better attested. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: how you can be saved
decisions.reason: Readable puts the noun as a verb. It keeps the sense of the meaning note, since "how" does not claim it is the only way.

decisions.choice: servants
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it; the meaning decision (m3) keeps that the person was owned, and Literal keeps "slave".

decisions.choice: esclavos (L); siervos (B, R)
decisions.reason: The term-sheet rendering, recorded once in this chapter, as the English: Literal shows that they are wholly owned by God (meaning decision m3); Balanced and Readable say "siervos", since slavery itself is not the point here.

decisions.choice: esclaves (L); serviteurs (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the term sheet settles for slaves of God: Literal keeps "esclaves", Balanced and Readable say "serviteurs", as the English does; the meaning decision (m3) keeps that they belonged wholly to God.

decisions.choice: watumwa (L); watumishi (B, R)
decisions.reason: The term-sheet rendering, recorded once in this chapter, as the English: Literal shows that they are wholly owned by God (meaning decision m3); Balanced and Readable say "watumishi", since slavery itself is not the point here.

decisions.choice: "Đức Chúa Trời Chí Cao" for the Most High God
decisions.reason: "Chí Cao" as in Luke 1:76 ("Đấng Chí Cao").

decisions.choice: the girl shouts to the passers-by in 해라체
decisions.reason: She cries out to the street, not to anyone in particular; the plain style suits a shout. "종들" at every level for the slaves of God, as in the Korean letters.

source.text: τοῦτο δὲ ἐποίει ἐπὶ πολλὰς ἡμέρας.

records.literal_gloss: This then she was doing for many days.

en.L: And she was doing this for many days.
en.B: She kept this up for many days.
en.R: She did this day after day for a long time.

es.L: Y esto hacía durante muchos días.
es.B: Así lo estuvo haciendo durante muchos días.
es.R: Hizo esto día tras día durante mucho tiempo.

fr.L: Et elle faisait cela pendant bien des jours.
fr.B: Elle continua ainsi pendant de nombreux jours.
fr.R: Elle a fait cela jour après jour, pendant longtemps.

sw.L: Na alikuwa akifanya hivyo siku nyingi.
sw.B: Aliendelea kufanya hivyo kwa siku nyingi.
sw.R: Alifanya hivyo siku baada ya siku kwa muda mrefu.

vi.L: Cô ta làm như vậy nhiều ngày.
vi.B: Cô ta cứ làm như thế nhiều ngày.
vi.R: Ngày nào cô cũng làm như vậy, suốt một thời gian dài.

ko.L: 그리고 그 여자는 여러 날 동안 이렇게 하고 있었다.
ko.B: 그 여자는 여러 날 동안 계속 그렇게 했다.
ko.R: 그 여자는 오랫동안 날마다 그렇게 했다.

decisions.choice: was doing: again and again
decisions.reason: The imperfect shows that it went on day after day.

source.text: διαπονηθεὶς δὲ Παῦλος καὶ ἐπιστρέψας τῷ πνεύματι εἶπεν· Παραγγέλλω σοι ἐν ὀνόματι Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ ἐξελθεῖν ἀπ’ αὐτῆς· καὶ ἐξῆλθεν αὐτῇ τῇ ὥρᾳ.

records.literal_gloss: Having been greatly troubled then Paul and having turned to the spirit said, I command you in name of Jesus Christ to come out from her; and it came out in the same hour.

en.L: But Paul, greatly troubled, turned and said to the spirit, "I command you in [the] name of Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} to come out of her." And it came out that very hour.
en.B: In the end Paul grew weary and vexed. He turned and told the spirit, "I order you in the name of Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} to come out of her!" It came out that same hour.
en.R: Paul became very upset. He turned around and said to the spirit, "By the power of Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, I order you to come out of her!" At once the spirit left her.

es.L: Pero Pablo, muy molesto, se volvió y dijo al espíritu: «Te ordeno en [el] nombre de {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}} que salgas de ella». Y salió en aquella misma hora.
es.B: Al final Pablo, cansado y molesto, se volvió y le dijo al espíritu: «¡En el nombre de {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}, te ordeno que salgas de ella!». Y en ese mismo momento salió.
es.R: Pablo se molestó mucho. Se dio vuelta y le dijo al espíritu: «¡Por el poder de {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}, te ordeno que salgas de ella!». Al instante el espíritu salió de ella.

fr.L: Mais Paul, très contrarié, se retourna et dit à l’esprit : « Je t’ordonne, au nom de Jésus {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, de sortir d’elle. » Et il sortit à l’heure même.
fr.B: À la fin, Paul, à bout de patience, se retourna et dit à l’esprit : « Je t’ordonne au nom de Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}} de sortir d’elle ! » Et l’esprit sortit à l’instant même.
fr.R: Paul en a eu assez. Il s’est retourné et a dit à l’esprit : « Par la puissance de Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}, je t’ordonne de sortir de cette fille ! » Aussitôt, l’esprit l’a quittée.

sw.L: Lakini Paulo, akiwa amechukizwa sana, aligeuka akamwambia yule pepo, "Nakuamuru kwa jina la Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} umtoke." Naye akamtoka saa ile ile.
sw.B: Mwishowe Paulo alichoshwa na kuudhika, akageuka, akamwambia yule pepo, "Nakuamuru kwa jina la Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}: mtoke msichana huyu!" Pepo huyo akamtoka saa ile ile.
sw.R: Paulo aliudhika sana. Akageuka, akamwambia yule pepo, "Kwa uwezo wa Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, nakuamuru umtoke msichana huyu!" Mara moja yule pepo akamtoka.

vi.L: Phao-lô bực mình, quay lại nói với linh ấy: "Nhân danh Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}}, ta truyền lệnh cho ngươi phải ra khỏi cô này." Và ngay giờ đó nó ra khỏi.
vi.B: Cuối cùng Phao-lô bực mình, quay lại bảo linh ấy: "Nhân danh Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}}, ta ra lệnh cho ngươi phải ra khỏi cô này!" Ngay giờ đó tà linh ra khỏi cô.
vi.R: Phao-lô rất bực. Ông quay lại nói với tà linh: "Bởi quyền năng của Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}}, ta ra lệnh cho ngươi phải ra khỏi cô này!" Lập tức tà linh ra khỏi cô.

ko.L: 그러자 바울이 몹시 괴로워하여 돌아서서 그 영에게 말했다. "내가 예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}의 이름으로 너에게 명령한다. 그 여자에게서 나오라." 그러자 바로 그 시간에 [영이] 나왔다.
ko.B: 마침내 바울은 몹시 괴로워하며 돌아서서 그 영에게 말했다. "예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}의 이름으로 너에게 명령한다. 그 여자에게서 나오너라!" 그러자 바로 그 순간 영이 나왔다.
ko.R: 바울은 몹시 괴로웠다. 그는 돌아서서 그 영에게 말했다. "예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}의 능력으로 너에게 명령한다. 그 여자에게서 나오너라!" 그러자 곧바로 영이 그 여자에게서 나갔다.

decisions.choice: greatly troubled: annoyed and worn down
decisions.reason: The verb means to be deeply disturbed or exasperated; the leaders were so with the apostles in 4:2. Luke does not say why: perhaps the noise, perhaps that a pagan spirit was announcing the message and confusing it.

decisions.choice: in the name of Jesus Christ: by his authority and power
decisions.reason: As in 3:6 and 3:16, the name stands for the person. In 19:13-16 those who use the name like a spell are overpowered.

decisions.choice: that very hour: at once
decisions.reason: An hour often means simply the moment (Luke 2:38, 7:21).

decisions.choice: by the power of
decisions.reason: Readable says what the name means here, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: in the end
decisions.reason: Balanced shows that his patience ran out after many days (16:18).

decisions.choice: {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}
decisions.reason: The English span covers only "Christ". Spanish writes the name as one word, "Jesucristo", so the span takes in the whole name, as the term sheet sets for every "Jesus Christ".

decisions.choice: Jésus {{christos:Christ|Messie}} (L); Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the style guide settles: without the hyphen of "Jésus-Christ", so that both options read naturally; Literal follows the Greek with no article, as the English Literal does.

decisions.choice: Paul says "ta" and "ngươi" to the spirit
decisions.reason: A command with authority to an evil spirit, not speech between people; "ta ... ngươi" is the form of a master to a subordinate, as Jesus' commands to spirits read in the Vietnamese Gospels.

source.text: Ἰδόντες δὲ οἱ κύριοι αὐτῆς ὅτι ἐξῆλθεν ἡ ἐλπὶς τῆς ἐργασίας αὐτῶν ἐπιλαβόμενοι τὸν Παῦλον καὶ τὸν Σιλᾶν εἵλκυσαν εἰς τὴν ἀγορὰν ἐπὶ τοὺς ἄρχοντας, καὶ προσαγαγόντες αὐτοὺς τοῖς στρατηγοῖς εἶπαν· Οὗτοι οἱ ἄνθρωποι ἐκταράσσουσιν ἡμῶν τὴν πόλιν Ἰουδαῖοι ὑπάρχοντες, καὶ καταγγέλλουσιν ἔθη ἃ οὐκ ἔξεστιν ἡμῖν παραδέχεσθαι οὐδὲ ποιεῖν Ῥωμαίοις οὖσιν.

records.literal_gloss: Having seen then the masters of her that went out the hope of the profit of them, having seized the Paul and the Silas they dragged [them] into the marketplace before the rulers, \v 20 and having brought them to the magistrates they said, These the men are throwing into confusion our the city, Jews being, \v 21 and they proclaim customs which not it is lawful for us to accept nor to practice, Romans being.

en.L: But when her masters saw that the hope of their profit had gone out, they seized Paul and Silas and dragged [them] into the marketplace before the rulers, \v 20 and bringing them to the magistrates, they said, "These men are throwing our city into confusion, being Jews, \v 21 and they proclaim customs that it is not lawful for us to accept or to practice, being Romans."
en.B: Her masters saw that their hope of gain had gone out of her along with the spirit. So they laid hold of Paul and Silas and hauled them off to the rulers in the marketplace. \v 20 Bringing them before the magistrates, they said, "These men are upsetting our whole city. They are Jews, \v 21 and they preach customs that we cannot lawfully take up or follow, since we are Romans."
en.R: The girl's owners saw that she could no longer make money for them. So they grabbed Paul and Silas and dragged them to the city leaders in the marketplace. \v 20 They brought them to the chief officials of the city and said, "These men are Jews, and they are causing a lot of trouble in our city. \v 21 They are teaching customs that we Romans are not allowed to accept or follow."

es.L: Pero al ver sus amos que había salido la esperanza de su ganancia, prendieron a Pablo y a Silas y [los] arrastraron a la plaza ante las autoridades, \v 20 y presentándolos a los magistrados, dijeron: «Estos hombres están alborotando nuestra ciudad, siendo judíos, \v 21 y anuncian costumbres que no nos es lícito aceptar ni practicar, siendo romanos».
es.B: Cuando sus amos vieron que, con el espíritu, había salido de ella también su esperanza de ganancia, agarraron a Pablo y a Silas y los arrastraron ante las autoridades en la plaza pública. \v 20 Los presentaron ante los magistrados y dijeron: «Estos hombres están alborotando toda nuestra ciudad. Son judíos, \v 21 y enseñan costumbres que a nosotros, como romanos, no nos está permitido adoptar ni practicar».
es.R: Los dueños de la muchacha vieron que ella ya no podía ganar dinero para ellos. Entonces agarraron a Pablo y a Silas y los llevaron a rastras ante los jefes de la ciudad, en la plaza. \v 20 Los llevaron ante los principales funcionarios de la ciudad y dijeron: «Estos hombres son judíos, y están causando muchos problemas en nuestra ciudad. \v 21 Enseñan costumbres que nosotros, los romanos, no podemos aceptar ni seguir».

fr.L: Mais ses maîtres, voyant que l’espoir de leur profit était sorti, saisirent Paul et Silas et [les] traînèrent sur la place publique devant les autorités, \v 20 et les ayant amenés aux magistrats, ils dirent : « Ces hommes jettent le trouble dans notre ville, étant Juifs, \v 21 et ils annoncent des coutumes qu’il ne nous est pas permis d’accepter ni de pratiquer, étant Romains. »
fr.B: Ses maîtres virent qu’avec l’esprit, l’espoir de leur gain était sorti d’elle. Ils s’emparèrent donc de Paul et de Silas et les traînèrent sur la place publique, devant les autorités. \v 20 Ils les présentèrent aux magistrats et dirent : « Ces hommes mettent toute notre ville en émoi. Ce sont des Juifs, \v 21 et ils prêchent des coutumes qu’il ne nous est pas permis d’adopter ni de suivre, à nous qui sommes Romains. »
fr.R: Les propriétaires de la jeune fille ont vu qu’elle ne pouvait plus leur faire gagner d’argent. Alors ils ont attrapé Paul et Silas et les ont traînés sur la grande place, devant les chefs de la ville. \v 20 Ils les ont amenés aux principaux responsables de la ville et ont dit : « Ces hommes sont des Juifs, et ils causent beaucoup de désordre dans notre ville. \v 21 Ils enseignent des coutumes que nous, les Romains, nous n’avons pas le droit d’accepter ni de suivre. »

sw.L: Lakini mabwana zake walipoona kwamba tumaini la faida yao limetoka, waliwakamata Paulo na Sila, wakawaburuta mpaka sokoni mbele ya watawala, \v 20 na wakiisha kuwaleta kwa mahakimu, walisema, "Watu hawa wanauvuruga mji wetu, wakiwa Wayahudi, \v 21 nao wanatangaza desturi ambazo si halali kwetu kuzipokea wala kuzifanya, tukiwa Warumi."
sw.B: Mabwana zake walipoona kwamba tumaini lao la kupata faida limetoka pamoja na yule pepo, waliwakamata Paulo na Sila, wakawaburuta mpaka kwa watawala kwenye uwanja wa soko. \v 20 Wakawaleta mbele ya mahakimu, wakasema, "Watu hawa wanauvuruga mji wetu wote. Wao ni Wayahudi, \v 21 nao wanafundisha desturi ambazo sisi, kwa kuwa ni Warumi, haturuhusiwi kisheria kuzikubali wala kuzifuata."
sw.R: Wamiliki wa yule msichana waliona kwamba hangeweza tena kuwapatia pesa. Basi wakawakamata Paulo na Sila, wakawaburuta mpaka kwa viongozi wa mji sokoni. \v 20 Wakawaleta mbele ya maafisa wakuu wa mji, wakasema, "Watu hawa ni Wayahudi, nao wanaleta fujo kubwa katika mji wetu. \v 21 Wanafundisha desturi ambazo sisi Warumi hatuna ruhusa kuzikubali wala kuzifuata."

vi.L: Các chủ của cô thấy hy vọng kiếm lời của mình đã mất, liền bắt Phao-lô và Si-la, kéo đến chợ trước mặt các nhà cầm quyền, \v 20 và giải họ đến trước các quan tòa, nói: "Những người này làm rối loạn thành chúng ta, họ là người Do Thái, \v 21 và họ truyền bá những tục lệ mà chúng ta là người La Mã không được phép chấp nhận hay làm theo."
vi.B: Các chủ của cô thấy hy vọng kiếm tiền của họ cũng đã ra đi cùng với tà linh, nên bắt Phao-lô và Si-la, kéo đến quảng trường trước mặt các nhà cầm quyền. \v 20 Họ giải hai người đến trước các quan tòa và nói: "Những người này đang làm náo loạn cả thành chúng ta. Họ là người Do Thái, \v 21 và họ truyền bá những tục lệ mà chúng ta là người La Mã không được phép theo hay thực hành."
vi.R: Các chủ của cô gái thấy cô không còn kiếm tiền cho họ được nữa. Vì vậy họ túm lấy Phao-lô và Si-la, kéo đến các nhà lãnh đạo thành ở quảng trường. \v 20 Họ đem hai người đến các quan chức đứng đầu thành và nói: "Những người này là người Do Thái, và họ đang gây rối loạn trong thành chúng ta. \v 21 Họ dạy những tục lệ mà người La Mã chúng ta không được phép chấp nhận hay làm theo."

ko.L: 그런데 그 여자의 주인들은 자기들의 돈벌이의 희망이 나가 버린 것을 보고, 바울과 실라를 붙잡아 장터로 관원들에게 끌고 갔다. \v 20 그리고 그들을 행정관들 앞에 데리고 가서 말했다. "이 사람들은 유대인인데, 우리 도시를 몹시 소란하게 하고 있습니다. \v 21 그리고 로마 사람인 우리가 받아들일 수도 없고 행할 수도 없는 풍습을 선전하고 있습니다."
ko.B: 그 여자의 주인들은 영과 함께 자기들의 돈벌이 희망도 나가 버린 것을 알았다. 그래서 바울과 실라를 붙잡아 장터에 있는 관원들에게 끌고 갔다. \v 20 그들은 두 사람을 행정관들 앞에 세우고 말했다. "이 사람들은 우리 도시를 온통 소란하게 하고 있습니다. 이들은 유대인인데, \v 21 로마 사람인 우리가 받아들일 수도 없고 따를 수도 없는 풍습을 퍼뜨리고 있습니다."
ko.R: 그 여자의 주인들은 이제 그 여자를 통해 돈을 벌 수 없게 된 것을 알았다. 그래서 바울과 실라를 붙잡아 장터에 있는 도시 지도자들에게 끌고 갔다. \v 20 그들은 두 사람을 도시의 높은 관리들 앞에 데려가서 말했다. "이 사람들은 유대인입니다. 그런데 우리 도시에 큰 소란을 일으키고 있습니다. \v 21 이들은 로마 사람인 우리가 받아들여서도 안 되고 따라서도 안 되는 풍습을 가르치고 있습니다."

decisions.choice: gone out: the same verb as for the spirit coming out
decisions.reason: The spirit "came out" (16:18) and the owners' hope of profit "went out" with it. The repeated verb makes a grim joke.

decisions.choice: rulers and magistrates: the same men, the chief officials of the colony
decisions.reason: "Rulers" is a general word for those in authority. "Magistrates" renders the Greek word for generals, which was used in Greek cities for the two chief officials who ran a Roman colony, known in Latin as duumvirs or praetors. Luke uses the word only of these officials from here on (16:22, 35, 36, 38).

decisions.choice: the marketplace: the forum, the city's public square
decisions.reason: The forum held the courts and offices of the city's officials. The foundations of the forum of Roman Philippi can still be seen.

decisions.choice: being Jews: an appeal to feeling against Jews
decisions.reason: The owners say nothing of their lost income. They set "Jews" against "Romans" (16:21). About this time the emperor Claudius ordered Jews out of Rome (18:2).

decisions.choice: customs not lawful for Romans: foreign religious ways that Romans should not take up
decisions.reason: Romans held that citizens should not adopt foreign cults that were not approved. The charge is vague, but it was serious in a colony that prided itself on being Roman.

decisions.choice: out of her along with the spirit
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the wordplay of the meaning note by saying what went out with what.

decisions.choice: the chief officials of the city
decisions.reason: Readable describes the office instead of naming it, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: she could no longer make money for them
alternatives: the hope of their profit had gone out
decisions.reason: Readable says what the loss was; the wordplay cannot be kept in plain words.

decisions.choice: las autoridades, los magistrados (L, B); los jefes de la ciudad, los principales funcionarios de la ciudad (R)
decisions.reason: Two words for the same chief officials of the colony (meaning decision m2). "Magistrados" is used for the second word through the rest of the chapter; "pretores", the Latin title, would need explaining. Readable says who they were, as the English does.

decisions.choice: les magistrats
decisions.reason: The Greek title stands for the two chief officials of a Roman colony (m2). "Les magistrats" is the plain French for such officials; "préteurs" is the Latin title and "stratèges" would suggest generals.

decisions.choice: watawala, mahakimu (L, B); viongozi wa mji, maafisa wakuu wa mji (R)
decisions.reason: Two words for the same chief officials of the colony (meaning decision m2). "Mahakimu" (magistrates) is used for the second word through the rest of the chapter, since these men also sat in judgment; Readable says who they were, as the English does.

decisions.choice: limetoka (L, B), as the spirit "akamtoka" (verse 18)
decisions.reason: Luke uses the same verb for the hope of profit going out as for the spirit coming out (meaning decision m1). Literal and Balanced keep "kutoka" so the play on words can still be heard; Readable says what it meant.

decisions.choice: "các quan tòa" (L, B); "các quan chức đứng đầu thành" (R) for the magistrates (16:20-38)
decisions.reason: The chief officials of the colony, who also judged (meaning decision); "quan tòa" names their part in this scene.

decisions.choice: inclusive "chúng ta" for the accusers and the magistrates
decisions.reason: The accusers speak as fellow citizens of the officials they address, so the inclusive form.

decisions.choice: "관원들" (L, B), "도시 지도자들" (R) for the rulers; "행정관들" (L, B), "도시의 높은 관리들", "도시 관리들" (R) for the magistrates (stratēgoi), through Acts 16
decisions.reason: The two words name the chief officials of the colony (meaning decision, uncertain). Korean keeps two words where the Greek has two; "행정관" says what the magistrates of a Roman colony were, and Readable uses plain words, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "희망이 나가 버린" (L); "영과 함께 자기들의 돈벌이 희망도 나가 버린" (B)
decisions.reason: The same verb is used for the spirit coming out (meaning decision); "나가다" keeps the link at Literal and Balanced, as the English does.

source.text: καὶ συνεπέστη ὁ ὄχλος κατ’ αὐτῶν, καὶ οἱ στρατηγοὶ περιρήξαντες αὐτῶν τὰ ἱμάτια ἐκέλευον ῥαβδίζειν, πολλάς τε ἐπιθέντες αὐτοῖς πληγὰς ἔβαλον εἰς φυλακήν, παραγγείλαντες τῷ δεσμοφύλακι ἀσφαλῶς τηρεῖν αὐτούς·

records.literal_gloss: And rose up together the crowd against them, and the magistrates having torn off of them the garments were ordering to beat with rods, \v 23 many and having laid on them blows they threw [them] into prison, having commanded the jailer securely to keep them;

en.L: And the crowd rose up together against them, and the magistrates, tearing off their garments, ordered [them] to be beaten with rods, \v 23 and after laying many blows on them, they threw [them] into prison, commanding the jailer to guard them securely.
en.B: The crowd too rose up against them, and the magistrates tore the clothes off them and ordered them beaten with rods. \v 23 When they had struck them many blows, they threw them into prison and told the jailer to keep them safely locked up.
en.R: A crowd of people joined in and turned against Paul and Silas. The city officials had their clothes torn off and ordered men to beat them with wooden rods. \v 23 They beat Paul and Silas many times. Then they threw them into prison and told the jailer to keep them locked up tight.

es.L: Y la multitud se levantó a una contra ellos, y los magistrados, rasgándoles las ropas, ordenaban que [los] azotaran con varas, \v 23 y después de darles muchos golpes, [los] echaron en la cárcel, mandando al carcelero que los guardara con seguridad.
es.B: También la multitud se levantó contra ellos, y los magistrados les arrancaron la ropa y ordenaron azotarlos con varas. \v 23 Después de darles muchos golpes, los echaron en la cárcel y ordenaron al carcelero que los vigilara con todo cuidado.
es.R: Mucha gente se unió y se puso en contra de Pablo y Silas. Los funcionarios de la ciudad mandaron que les quitaran la ropa y ordenaron a unos hombres que los golpearan con varas de madera. \v 23 Golpearon a Pablo y a Silas muchas veces. Luego los echaron en la cárcel y le dijeron al carcelero que los tuviera bien encerrados.

fr.L: Et la foule se souleva aussi contre eux, et les magistrats, leur ayant arraché leurs vêtements, ordonnèrent de [les] battre de verges, \v 23 et leur ayant donné beaucoup de coups, ils [les] jetèrent en prison, ordonnant au geôlier de les garder avec soin.
fr.B: La foule se souleva elle aussi contre eux, et les magistrats leur arrachèrent leurs vêtements et ordonnèrent de les battre de verges. \v 23 Après les avoir roués de coups, ils les jetèrent en prison et ordonnèrent au geôlier de les surveiller étroitement.
fr.R: La foule s’est mise elle aussi contre Paul et Silas. Les responsables de la ville leur ont fait arracher leurs vêtements et ont ordonné qu’on les frappe avec des bâtons. \v 23 On a frappé Paul et Silas de nombreux coups. Puis on les a jetés en prison, et on a ordonné au gardien de la prison de bien les enfermer.

sw.L: Na umati ukainuka pamoja dhidi yao, na mahakimu, wakiwararulia mavazi yao, waliamuru wapigwe kwa fimbo, \v 23 na baada ya kuwapiga mapigo mengi, waliwatupa gerezani, wakimwagiza mlinzi wa gereza awalinde kwa uthabiti.
sw.B: Umati wa watu nao uliinuka dhidi yao, na mahakimu wakawararulia nguo zao, wakaamuru wachapwe kwa fimbo. \v 23 Baada ya kuwachapa mapigo mengi, waliwatupa gerezani, wakamwagiza mlinzi wa gereza awalinde kwa uangalifu wasitoroke.
sw.R: Watu wengi pia walijiunga, wakawageukia Paulo na Sila. Maafisa wa mji waliamuru nguo zao zivuliwe, wakaamuru watu wawapige kwa fimbo za mti. \v 23 Waliwapiga Paulo na Sila mara nyingi. Kisha wakawatupa gerezani, wakamwambia mlinzi wa gereza awafungie ndani kwa uangalifu mkubwa.

vi.L: Đám đông cũng nổi dậy chống lại họ, và các quan tòa xé áo họ ra và ra lệnh đánh bằng roi; \v 23 sau khi đã đánh họ nhiều đòn, họ ném vào ngục, truyền cho viên cai ngục canh giữ họ cẩn thận;
vi.B: Đám đông cũng nổi lên chống lại hai người. Các quan tòa xé áo họ ra và ra lệnh đánh đòn họ bằng roi. \v 23 Sau khi đánh họ nhiều đòn, các quan ném họ vào ngục và truyền cho viên cai ngục canh giữ họ thật cẩn thận.
vi.R: Đám đông cũng hùa vào chống lại Phao-lô và Si-la. Các quan chức cho lột áo hai người ra và ra lệnh lấy roi gỗ đánh họ. \v 23 Họ bị đánh rất nhiều đòn. Rồi các quan ném họ vào ngục và bảo viên cai ngục phải canh giữ họ thật chặt.

ko.L: 그러자 무리도 함께 일어나 그들을 대적했다. 그리고 행정관들은 그들의 옷을 찢어 벗기고 막대기로 때리라고 명령했다. \v 23 그리고 그들에게 매를 많이 때린 뒤에 감옥에 가두고, 간수에게 그들을 단단히 지키라고 명령했다.
ko.B: 무리도 덩달아 그들에게 달려들었다. 행정관들은 그들의 옷을 찢어 벗기고 막대기로 때리라고 명령했다. \v 23 그들은 두 사람에게 매를 많이 때린 뒤에 감옥에 가두고, 간수에게 그들을 단단히 지키라고 명령했다.
ko.R: 많은 사람이 몰려와 함께 바울과 실라를 공격했다. 도시 관리들은 그들의 옷을 찢어 벗기게 하고, 사람들에게 나무 막대기로 그들을 때리라고 명령했다. \v 23 사람들은 바울과 실라를 여러 번 때렸다. 그리고 그들을 감옥에 가두고, 간수에게 그들이 도망가지 못하게 잘 지키라고 명령했다.

decisions.choice: tearing off their garments: stripping Paul and Silas for the beating
alternatives: the magistrates tearing their own robes in outrage
decisions.reason: The pronoun could refer to the magistrates, but a Roman beating was given on the bare back, and the magistrates order it at once. The officials gave the order; their attendants did the stripping.

decisions.choice: beaten with rods: the Roman punishment carried out by the magistrates' attendants
decisions.reason: The attendants of Roman magistrates, the lictors, carried bundles of rods (16:35). Paul says he was beaten with rods three times (2 Corinthians 11:25) and speaks of being shamefully treated at Philippi (1 Thessalonians 2:2).

decisions.choice: guard them securely: keep them so they could not escape
decisions.reason: The adverb means safely or surely; the next verse shows what the jailer did to make sure.

decisions.choice: ordered men to beat them with wooden rods
alternatives: ordered them to be beaten with rods
decisions.reason: Readable says that others carried out the beating, and what the rods were.

decisions.choice: las ropas (L); la ropa (B, R)
decisions.reason: The term sheet keeps "manto" for the outer cloak, but here the word means their clothes in general, stripped off for the beating (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: mlinzi wa gereza (every level, through the chapter)
decisions.reason: The word means the man who kept the prisoners. "Mkuu wa gereza" would make him the head of a modern prison service; "mlinzi wa gereza" says plainly what he did.

decisions.choice: "viên cai ngục" for the jailer
decisions.reason: The plain word for the officer in charge of a prison.

source.text: ὃς παραγγελίαν τοιαύτην λαβὼν ἔβαλεν αὐτοὺς εἰς τὴν ἐσωτέραν φυλακὴν καὶ τοὺς πόδας ἠσφαλίσατο αὐτῶν εἰς τὸ ξύλον.

records.literal_gloss: who an order such having received threw them into the inner prison and the feet fastened of them in the wood.

en.L: Having received such an order, he threw them into the inner prison and fastened their feet in the stocks.
en.B: Given such a charge, the jailer threw them into the inner part of the prison and made their feet fast in the stocks.
en.R: Because of this order, the jailer put them in a room deep inside the prison. He locked their feet between heavy blocks of wood so they could not move.

es.L: El cual, habiendo recibido tal orden, los echó en la cárcel de más adentro y les sujetó los pies en el cepo.
es.B: Al recibir esa orden, el carcelero los metió en la parte más interior de la cárcel y les aseguró los pies en el cepo.
es.R: Por esa orden, el carcelero los puso en un cuarto muy adentro de la cárcel. Les encerró los pies entre unos bloques pesados de madera para que no pudieran moverse.

fr.L: Celui-ci, ayant reçu un tel ordre, les jeta dans la prison intérieure et leur fixa les pieds dans les ceps.
fr.B: Sur un tel ordre, le geôlier les jeta au fond de la prison et leur bloqua les pieds dans des entraves de bois.
fr.R: À cause de cet ordre, le gardien les a mis dans une cellule tout au fond de la prison. Il a bloqué leurs pieds entre de lourdes pièces de bois, pour qu’ils ne puissent plus bouger.

sw.L: Naye, akiisha kupokea agizo kama hilo, aliwatupa katika gereza la ndani, akaifunga miguu yao katika mkatale.
sw.B: Mlinzi wa gereza alipopewa agizo hilo, aliwatia katika chumba cha ndani kabisa cha gereza, akaifunga miguu yao kwa mkatale.
sw.R: Kwa sababu ya agizo hilo, mlinzi wa gereza aliwaweka katika chumba kilichokuwa ndani kabisa ya gereza. Akaifungia miguu yao kati ya vipande vizito vya mti ili wasiweze kusogea.

vi.L: Nhận được lệnh như vậy, người ấy ném họ vào ngục trong và xiềng chân họ vào cùm.
vi.B: Nhận được lệnh như vậy, viên cai ngục ném họ vào phòng giam trong cùng và cùm chân họ lại.
vi.R: Vì lệnh ấy, viên cai ngục đưa họ vào một phòng giam sâu bên trong nhà ngục. Ông kẹp chân họ giữa những khúc gỗ nặng để họ không cử động được.

ko.L: 그는 이런 명령을 받고, 그들을 깊은 감옥에 가두고 그들의 발에 차꼬를 단단히 채웠다.
ko.B: 이런 명령을 받은 간수는 그들을 감옥 깊숙한 곳에 가두고 그들의 발에 차꼬를 단단히 채웠다.
ko.R: 이 명령을 받은 간수는 그들을 감옥 맨 안쪽 방에 가두었다. 그리고 그들이 움직이지 못하도록 무거운 나무 틀에 그들의 발을 끼워 채웠다.

decisions.choice: the stocks: a wooden frame that held the feet fast
decisions.reason: The word means wood. Stocks had holes for the legs and could be set to spread them painfully apart. With their backs torn from the beating, the prisoners could neither move nor lie easily.

decisions.choice: the inner prison: the innermost, most secure cell
decisions.reason: The jailer chose the place hardest to escape from, as ordered (16:23).

decisions.choice: between heavy blocks of wood so they could not move
decisions.reason: Readable describes the stocks.

decisions.choice: the jailer
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the subject; the Greek joins this to the last sentence with "who".

decisions.choice: les ceps (L); des entraves de bois (B); a description (R)
decisions.reason: "Les ceps" is the French term for stocks but is now rare; Literal keeps it, Balanced says what they were made of, and Readable describes them, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "차꼬" (L, B); "무거운 나무 틀" (R) for the stocks
decisions.reason: "차꼬" is the Korean word for the wooden frame that held the feet (meaning decision); "족쇄" is an iron fetter. Readable describes it.

source.text: Κατὰ δὲ τὸ μεσονύκτιον Παῦλος καὶ Σιλᾶς προσευχόμενοι ὕμνουν τὸν θεόν, ἐπηκροῶντο δὲ αὐτῶν οἱ δέσμιοι·

records.literal_gloss: About then the midnight Paul and Silas praying were singing hymns to the God, were listening and to them the prisoners.

en.L: And about midnight Paul and Silas, praying, were singing hymns to God, and the prisoners were listening to them.
en.B: At midnight, as Paul and Silas prayed, they sang praises to God, and the prisoners listened.
en.R: Around midnight Paul and Silas prayed and sang songs to praise God. The other prisoners in the jail heard them.

es.L: Y como a medianoche, Pablo y Silas, orando, cantaban himnos a Dios, y los presos los escuchaban.
es.B: A medianoche, mientras oraban, Pablo y Silas cantaban alabanzas a Dios, y los presos los escuchaban.
es.R: Cerca de la medianoche, Pablo y Silas oraban y cantaban canciones para alabar a Dios. Los otros presos de la cárcel los oían.

fr.L: Et vers minuit, Paul et Silas, priant, chantaient des hymnes à Dieu, et les prisonniers les écoutaient.
fr.B: Vers minuit, Paul et Silas, en priant, chantaient la louange de Dieu, et les prisonniers les écoutaient.
fr.R: Vers minuit, Paul et Silas ont prié et ils ont chanté des chants pour louer Dieu. Les autres prisonniers les entendaient.

sw.L: Na yapata usiku wa manane Paulo na Sila, wakiomba, walikuwa wakimwimbia Mungu nyimbo za sifa, na wafungwa walikuwa wakiwasikiliza.
sw.B: Usiku wa manane, Paulo na Sila walipokuwa wakiomba, walimwimbia Mungu nyimbo za sifa, na wafungwa walikuwa wakiwasikiliza.
sw.R: Karibu na usiku wa manane Paulo na Sila waliomba na kuimba nyimbo za kumsifu Mungu. Wafungwa wengine gerezani waliwasikia.

vi.L: Khoảng nửa đêm, Phao-lô và Si-la đang cầu nguyện và hát thánh ca ngợi khen Đức Chúa Trời, các tù nhân đều lắng nghe họ.
vi.B: Vào lúc nửa đêm, Phao-lô và Si-la cầu nguyện và hát thánh ca ca ngợi Đức Chúa Trời, và các tù nhân đều lắng nghe.
vi.R: Khoảng nửa đêm, Phao-lô và Si-la cầu nguyện và hát những bài ca ngợi khen Đức Chúa Trời. Các tù nhân khác trong ngục đều nghe họ hát.

ko.L: 그런데 한밤중쯤에 바울과 실라가 기도하면서 하나님을 찬양하는 노래를 부르고 있었고, 죄수들이 그들의 [노래를] 듣고 있었다.
ko.B: 한밤중에 바울과 실라는 기도하며 하나님께 찬송을 부르고 있었다. 그리고 다른 죄수들이 그 노래를 듣고 있었다.
ko.R: 한밤중쯤에 바울과 실라는 기도하고, 하나님을 찬양하는 노래를 불렀다. 감옥에 있던 다른 죄수들도 그 노래를 들었다.

decisions.choice: praying, singing hymns: prayer that took the form of song
decisions.reason: The participle and the verb go together: their prayer was sung praise, as in many Psalms.

decisions.choice: singing hymns: singing praise to God
decisions.reason: The verb is used of Jesus and the disciples singing after the last supper (Mark 14:26), probably Psalms.

decisions.choice: were listening: listening closely
decisions.reason: The verb means to listen attentively, as to a performance.

decisions.choice: the other prisoners in the jail
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that these were the others held there.

source.text: ἄφνω δὲ σεισμὸς ἐγένετο μέγας ὥστε σαλευθῆναι τὰ θεμέλια τοῦ δεσμωτηρίου, ἠνεῴχθησαν δὲ παραχρῆμα αἱ θύραι πᾶσαι, καὶ πάντων τὰ δεσμὰ ἀνέθη.

records.literal_gloss: Suddenly then earthquake happened great so that were shaken the foundations of the prison; were opened then immediately the doors all, and of all the chains were unfastened.

en.L: And suddenly there was a great earthquake, so that the foundations of the prison were shaken; and immediately all the doors were opened, and the chains of all were unfastened.
en.B: All at once a great earthquake struck, so strong that the prison was shaken to its foundations. In that instant all the doors came open, and the chains of every prisoner fell loose.
en.R: Suddenly there was a strong earthquake. It shook the prison down to its foundations. Right away all the doors of the prison opened, and the chains fell off all the prisoners.

es.L: Y de repente hubo un gran terremoto, de modo que fueron sacudidos los cimientos de la cárcel; y al instante se abrieron todas las puertas, y las cadenas de todos se soltaron.
es.B: De pronto se produjo un terremoto tan fuerte que la cárcel se estremeció hasta los cimientos. En ese mismo instante se abrieron todas las puertas, y a todos los presos se les soltaron las cadenas.
es.R: De repente hubo un terremoto muy fuerte. Sacudió la cárcel hasta los cimientos. Enseguida se abrieron todas las puertas de la cárcel, y a todos los presos se les cayeron las cadenas.

fr.L: Et soudain il se produisit un grand tremblement de terre, si bien que les fondations de la prison furent ébranlées ; et aussitôt toutes les portes s’ouvrirent, et les liens de tous furent détachés.
fr.B: Tout à coup, un violent tremblement de terre secoua la prison jusque dans ses fondations. Au même instant, toutes les portes s’ouvrirent et les chaînes de tous les prisonniers se détachèrent.
fr.R: Tout à coup, il y a eu un fort tremblement de terre. Il a secoué la prison jusqu’à ses fondations. Aussitôt, toutes les portes de la prison se sont ouvertes, et les chaînes de tous les prisonniers sont tombées.

sw.L: Na ghafla palitokea tetemeko kuu la nchi, hata misingi ya gereza ikatikisika; na mara moja milango yote ikafunguka, na vifungo vya wote vikafunguliwa.
sw.B: Ghafla kulitokea tetemeko kubwa la nchi, kiasi kwamba gereza likatikiswa hadi misingi yake. Papo hapo milango yote ikafunguka, na minyororo ya kila mfungwa ikaachia.
sw.R: Ghafla kulitokea tetemeko kubwa la nchi. Lilitikisa gereza hadi kwenye misingi yake. Mara moja milango yote ya gereza ikafunguka, na minyororo ikaanguka kutoka kwa wafungwa wote.

vi.L: Thình lình có một trận động đất lớn, đến nỗi nền nhà ngục rung chuyển; lập tức tất cả các cửa đều mở ra, và xiềng xích của mọi người đều tuột ra.
vi.B: Bỗng nhiên có một trận động đất lớn, mạnh đến nỗi nhà ngục rung chuyển tận nền móng. Ngay lúc đó, mọi cửa ngục đều mở tung, và xiềng xích của mọi tù nhân đều tuột ra.
vi.R: Bỗng có một trận động đất rất mạnh. Nhà ngục rung chuyển đến tận nền móng. Ngay lập tức tất cả các cửa ngục đều mở ra, và xiềng xích rơi khỏi mọi tù nhân.

ko.L: 그런데 갑자기 큰 지진이 일어나서 감옥의 기초가 흔들렸다. 그리고 곧 모든 문이 열리고, 모든 사람의 사슬이 풀렸다.
ko.B: 그때 갑자기 큰 지진이 일어나서 감옥의 기초가 흔들렸다. 그 순간 감옥 문이 모두 열리고, 죄수들을 묶었던 사슬이 다 풀렸다.
ko.R: 갑자기 강한 지진이 일어났다. 그 지진으로 감옥이 기초까지 흔들렸다. 곧바로 감옥 문이 모두 열리고, 죄수들을 묶고 있던 사슬이 다 풀려 버렸다.

decisions.choice: the earthquake: God's answer, freeing his servants
decisions.reason: Luke does not say so in words, but God frees his messengers from prison in 5:19 and 12:7-10, and an earthquake follows prayer in 4:31. Even so, Paul and Silas do not run.

decisions.choice: the chains were unfastened: came loose from what held them
decisions.reason: Chains were fixed to the walls or the stocks; the shaking loosened the fastenings.

source.text: ἔξυπνος δὲ γενόμενος ὁ δεσμοφύλαξ καὶ ἰδὼν ἀνεῳγμένας τὰς θύρας τῆς φυλακῆς σπασάμενος τὴν μάχαιραν ἤμελλεν ἑαυτὸν ἀναιρεῖν, νομίζων ἐκπεφευγέναι τοὺς δεσμίους.

records.literal_gloss: Awake then having become the jailer and having seen opened the doors of the prison, having drawn the sword he was about himself to kill, supposing to have escaped the prisoners.

en.L: And the jailer, waking up and seeing the doors of the prison opened, drew [his] sword and was about to kill himself, supposing that the prisoners had escaped.
en.B: Startled out of sleep, the jailer saw that the prison doors stood open. Believing that the prisoners had got away, he drew his sword, ready to take his own life.
en.R: The jailer woke up and saw that the doors of the prison were open. He thought the prisoners had run away. So he pulled out his sword to kill himself.

es.L: Y el carcelero, despertándose y viendo abiertas las puertas de la cárcel, sacando la espada, iba a matarse, pensando que los presos se habían escapado.
es.B: El carcelero despertó sobresaltado y vio abiertas las puertas de la cárcel. Creyendo que los presos se habían escapado, sacó la espada, dispuesto a quitarse la vida.
es.R: El carcelero se despertó y vio que las puertas de la cárcel estaban abiertas. Pensó que los presos se habían escapado. Entonces sacó su espada para matarse.

fr.L: Et le geôlier, s’étant réveillé et voyant ouvertes les portes de la prison, tira l’épée et allait se tuer, pensant que les prisonniers s’étaient enfuis.
fr.B: Tiré de son sommeil, le geôlier vit que les portes de la prison étaient ouvertes. Croyant que les prisonniers s’étaient enfuis, il tira son épée et s’apprêta à se donner la mort.
fr.R: Le gardien s’est réveillé et a vu que les portes de la prison étaient ouvertes. Il a pensé que les prisonniers s’étaient enfuis. Alors il a sorti son épée pour se tuer.

sw.L: Na mlinzi wa gereza, akiamka na kuona milango ya gereza imefunguliwa, aliuchomoa upanga [wake], akawa karibu kujiua, akidhani kwamba wafungwa wamekimbia.
sw.B: Mlinzi wa gereza aliamka kwa mshtuko, akaona milango ya gereza iko wazi. Akidhani kwamba wafungwa wametoroka, akauchomoa upanga wake, tayari kujiua.
sw.R: Mlinzi wa gereza aliamka, akaona kwamba milango ya gereza ilikuwa wazi. Alidhani kwamba wafungwa walikuwa wamekimbia. Basi akauchomoa upanga wake ili ajiue.

vi.L: Viên cai ngục thức dậy, thấy các cửa ngục đều mở, rút gươm định tự sát, vì tưởng các tù nhân đã trốn mất.
vi.B: Viên cai ngục giật mình thức dậy, thấy các cửa ngục đều mở toang. Tưởng rằng các tù nhân đã trốn thoát, ông rút gươm ra định tự sát.
vi.R: Viên cai ngục thức dậy và thấy các cửa ngục đều mở. Ông tưởng các tù nhân đã trốn đi hết. Vì vậy ông rút gươm ra để tự giết mình.

ko.L: 그리고 간수가 잠에서 깨어 감옥 문들이 열려 있는 것을 보고, 죄수들이 도망친 줄로 생각하여 칼을 빼서 자결하려고 했다.
ko.B: 간수가 잠에서 깨어 보니 감옥 문들이 열려 있었다. 그는 죄수들이 다 도망친 줄 알고 칼을 빼서 스스로 목숨을 끊으려고 했다.
ko.R: 간수는 잠에서 깨어 감옥 문들이 열려 있는 것을 보았다. 그는 죄수들이 모두 도망갔다고 생각했다. 그래서 칼을 빼서 자기 목숨을 끊으려고 했다.

decisions.choice: about to kill himself: he expected to die for the escape
decisions.reason: A guard who let prisoners escape could suffer the penalty they would have suffered (12:19, 27:42). The jailer chose death by his own hand over trial and disgrace.

decisions.choice: supposing: he assumed it, without looking
decisions.reason: In the dark he saw the open doors and drew the obvious conclusion.

source.text: ἐφώνησεν δὲ φωνῇ μεγάλῃ ὁ Παῦλος λέγων· Μηδὲν πράξῃς σεαυτῷ κακόν, ἅπαντες γάρ ἐσμεν ἐνθάδε.

records.literal_gloss: Called out but with a voice loud the Paul saying, Nothing do to yourself harm, all for we are here.

en.L: But Paul called out with a loud voice, saying, "Do yourself no harm, for we are all here."
en.B: But Paul shouted at the top of his voice, "Do not hurt yourself! Every one of us is still here!"
en.R: But Paul shouted loudly, "Do not hurt yourself! We are all still here!"

es.L: Pero Pablo gritó con gran voz, diciendo: «No te hagas ningún mal, porque todos estamos aquí».
es.B: Pero Pablo le gritó con todas sus fuerzas: «¡No te hagas daño! ¡Todos estamos todavía aquí!».
es.R: Pero Pablo gritó muy fuerte: «¡No te hagas daño! ¡Todos seguimos aquí!».

fr.L: Mais Paul cria d’une voix forte, disant : « Ne te fais aucun mal, car nous sommes tous ici. »
fr.B: Mais Paul cria de toutes ses forces : « Ne te fais pas de mal ! Nous sommes tous encore là ! »
fr.R: Mais Paul a crié très fort : « Ne te fais pas de mal ! Nous sommes tous encore ici ! »

sw.L: Lakini Paulo aliita kwa sauti kuu, akisema, "Usijidhuru hata kidogo, kwa maana sisi sote tuko hapa."
sw.B: Lakini Paulo alipaza sauti kwa nguvu zake zote, "Usijidhuru! Sisi sote bado tuko hapa!"
sw.R: Lakini Paulo alipiga kelele kwa sauti kubwa, "Usijiumize! Sote bado tuko hapa!"

vi.L: Nhưng Phao-lô kêu lớn tiếng rằng: "Đừng làm hại mình, vì tất cả chúng tôi đều ở đây."
vi.B: Nhưng Phao-lô kêu lớn: "Đừng làm hại mình! Tất cả chúng tôi vẫn còn ở đây!"
vi.R: Nhưng Phao-lô kêu lớn: "Ông đừng làm hại mình! Tất cả chúng tôi vẫn còn ở đây!"

ko.L: 그러나 바울이 큰 소리로 외쳐 말했다. "당신 몸을 해치지 마십시오. 우리가 모두 여기 있습니다."
ko.B: 그러나 바울이 큰 소리로 외쳤다. "당신 몸을 해치지 마십시오! 우리가 모두 그대로 여기 있습니다!"
ko.R: 그러나 바울이 크게 소리쳤다. "스스로 해치지 마십시오! 우리는 모두 아직 여기 있습니다!"

decisions.choice: all: all the prisoners, not only Paul and Silas
decisions.reason: The jailer feared that the prisoners had escaped (16:27). Paul tells him none has. Luke does not say why the others stayed.

decisions.choice: do yourself no harm: a command not to go through with it
decisions.reason: The aorist with "no" forbids an act about to be done.

decisions.choice: still here
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable bring out that no one had left.

decisions.choice: "Ông" for the jailer in Paul's mouth (R); Paul and Silas say "chúng tôi"
decisions.reason: The jailer is an officer, and Paul speaks to him with plain respect; Literal and Balanced need no pronoun, as Vietnamese commands often have none.

decisions.choice: Paul speaks to the jailer in 합쇼체, with "당신" (L, B) for "yourself"
decisions.reason: The jailer is a stranger and an official; Paul's urgent call is still respectful. "당신" is the polite pronoun for a person one does not know, used here because Korean needs a word for "yourself"; Readable says "스스로".

source.text: αἰτήσας δὲ φῶτα εἰσεπήδησεν καὶ ἔντρομος γενόμενος προσέπεσεν τῷ Παύλῳ καὶ τῷ Σιλᾷ, καὶ προαγαγὼν αὐτοὺς ἔξω ἔφη· Κύριοι, τί με δεῖ ποιεῖν ἵνα σωθῶ;

records.literal_gloss: Having asked for then lights he rushed in, and trembling having become he fell down before the Paul and the Silas, \v 30 and having brought them outside he was saying, Sirs, what me is it necessary to do that I may be saved?

en.L: And asking for lights, he rushed in, and becoming terrified, he fell down before Paul and Silas, \v 30 and bringing them outside, he said, "Sirs, what must I do that I may be saved?"
en.B: He called for lights and ran inside, and shaking with fear he fell at the feet of Paul and Silas. \v 30 He led them out and said, "Sirs, what must I do to be saved?"
en.R: The jailer asked for lamps and ran into the prison. He was shaking with fear, and he bowed down in front of Paul and Silas. \v 30 Then he brought them outside and asked, "Sirs, what do I need to do to be saved?"

es.L: Y pidiendo luces, se precipitó adentro, y temblando, se postró ante Pablo y Silas, \v 30 y sacándolos fuera, dijo: «Señores, ¿qué me es necesario hacer para ser salvo?».
es.B: Pidió luz, entró corriendo y, temblando de miedo, se echó a los pies de Pablo y Silas. \v 30 Luego los sacó fuera y les preguntó: «Señores, ¿qué tengo que hacer para ser salvo?».
es.R: El carcelero pidió lámparas y entró corriendo a la cárcel. Temblaba de miedo, y se arrodilló delante de Pablo y Silas. \v 30 Después los sacó afuera y les preguntó: «Señores, ¿qué necesito hacer para ser salvo?».

fr.L: Ayant demandé des lumières, il se précipita à l’intérieur, et tout tremblant, il tomba devant Paul et Silas, \v 30 et les ayant fait sortir, il dit : « Messieurs, que me faut-il faire pour être sauvé ? »
fr.B: Il demanda de la lumière, se précipita à l’intérieur et, tremblant de peur, se jeta aux pieds de Paul et de Silas. \v 30 Puis il les fit sortir et leur dit : « Messieurs, que dois-je faire pour être sauvé ? »
fr.R: Le gardien a demandé des lampes et il a couru dans la prison. Il tremblait de peur, et il s’est jeté à genoux devant Paul et Silas. \v 30 Ensuite, il les a fait sortir et leur a demandé : « Messieurs, qu’est-ce que je dois faire pour être sauvé ? »

sw.L: Na akiomba taa, aliingia ndani mbio, na akiwa anatetemeka, akaanguka mbele ya Paulo na Sila, \v 30 na akiwatoa nje, alisema, "Mabwana, imenipasa kufanya nini ili niokolewe?"
sw.B: Aliagiza taa ziletwe, akaingia ndani mbio, na huku akitetemeka kwa hofu akaanguka mbele ya Paulo na Sila. \v 30 Akawatoa nje, akasema, "Mabwana, nifanye nini ili niokolewe?"
sw.R: Mlinzi wa gereza aliomba taa, akakimbia ndani ya gereza. Alikuwa akitetemeka kwa hofu, akainama mbele ya Paulo na Sila. \v 30 Kisha akawatoa nje, akauliza, "Mabwana, ninahitaji kufanya nini ili niokolewe?"

vi.L: Người ấy xin đèn, chạy vào, run rẩy sấp mình trước Phao-lô và Si-la, \v 30 rồi dẫn họ ra ngoài và nói: "Thưa các ông, tôi phải làm gì để được cứu?"
vi.B: Viên cai ngục gọi lấy đèn, chạy vào, run rẩy quỳ sụp dưới chân Phao-lô và Si-la. \v 30 Rồi ông dẫn hai người ra ngoài và hỏi: "Thưa các ông, tôi phải làm gì để được cứu?"
vi.R: Viên cai ngục bảo người ta mang đèn đến, rồi chạy vào trong ngục. Ông run sợ và quỳ xuống trước mặt Phao-lô và Si-la. \v 30 Rồi ông dẫn hai người ra ngoài và hỏi: "Thưa các ông, tôi cần phải làm gì để được cứu?"

ko.L: 그러자 그는 등불을 달라고 하여 뛰어 들어가서, 두려워 떨며 바울과 실라 앞에 엎드렸다. \v 30 그리고 그들을 밖으로 데리고 나와서 말했다. "선생님들, 내가 구원을 받으려면 어떻게 해야 합니까?"
ko.B: 간수는 등불을 가져오게 하고 안으로 뛰어 들어가, 두려워 떨면서 바울과 실라 앞에 엎드렸다. \v 30 그리고 그들을 밖으로 데리고 나와서 말했다. "선생님들, 제가 구원을 받으려면 어떻게 해야 합니까?"
ko.R: 간수는 등불을 가져오라고 하고 감옥 안으로 뛰어 들어갔다. 그는 두려워서 떨며 바울과 실라 앞에 엎드렸다. \v 30 그리고 그들을 밖으로 데리고 나와서 물었다. "선생님들, 제가 구원을 받으려면 어떻게 해야 합니까?"

decisions.choice: fell down before: a sign of awe and fear
decisions.reason: He bows before the men he now sees as servants of a powerful God, as Cornelius did before Peter (10:25). They do not refuse it here, but they point him at once to the Lord Jesus (16:31).

decisions.choice: Sirs: a respectful address
decisions.reason: The word is the plural of "lord" and was a polite way to address men of standing. It is the same word used of the slave girl's masters (16:16, 16:19).

decisions.choice: be saved: rescued by God, in the full sense Paul gives it in his answer
decisions.reason: The jailer may have meant more or less than he knew. The slave girl had announced "a way of salvation" (16:17) for days in the city, and the earthquake had shown God's power. Paul and Silas answer with salvation through the Lord Jesus (16:31).

decisions.choice: lamps
decisions.reason: Readable names the kind of light he would have used.

decisions.choice: Señores
decisions.reason: The plural of the polite "señor" (meaning decision m2), as the term sheet sets for this address. It is capitalised only because it begins his question; it is not the title "Lord".

decisions.choice: Messieurs
decisions.reason: As in John, the respectful address is "Monsieur" from someone who does not yet believe (m2); "Seigneurs" would give it a religious sense it does not have here.

decisions.choice: Mabwana
decisions.reason: The plural of the polite "bwana", a respectful address (meaning decision m2), as the term sheet sets for "sir". It is not "Bwana", the Lord; the capital comes only from the start of his question.

decisions.choice: "Thưa các ông" for "Sirs"
decisions.reason: A respectful address (meaning decision); "các ông" is respectful without the deference "các ngài" gives to high officials.

decisions.choice: "선생님들" for kyrioi, with "나" (L) and "제" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The word is a respectful address (meaning decision), not "lords"; "선생님" is the Korean courtesy for respected men, as for kyrie said to Jesus as "선생님" where it is polite in the Korean John.

source.text: οἱ δὲ εἶπαν· Πίστευσον ἐπὶ τὸν κύριον Ἰησοῦν, καὶ σωθήσῃ σὺ καὶ ὁ οἶκός σου.

records.literal_gloss: They then said, Believe on the Lord Jesus, and you will be saved, you and the household of you.

en.L: And they said, "Believe on the Lord Jesus, and you will be saved, you and your household."
en.B: They answered, "Believe in the Lord Jesus, and you will be saved, you and your household."
en.R: They said, "Believe in the Lord Jesus. Then you will be saved, and so will the people in your home."

es.L: Y ellos dijeron: «Cree en el Señor Jesús, y serás salvo, tú y tu casa».
es.B: Ellos le respondieron: «Cree en el Señor Jesús, y serás salvo, tú y los de tu casa».
es.R: Ellos le dijeron: «Cree en el Señor Jesús. Entonces serás salvo, y también los que viven en tu casa».

fr.L: Et ils dirent : « Crois au Seigneur Jésus, et tu seras sauvé, toi et ta maison. »
fr.B: Ils répondirent : « Crois au Seigneur Jésus, et tu seras sauvé, toi et ta famille. »
fr.R: Ils lui ont répondu : « Crois au Seigneur Jésus. Alors tu seras sauvé, et les gens de ta maison aussi. »

sw.L: Nao wakasema, "Amini katika Bwana Yesu, nawe utaokolewa, wewe na nyumba yako."
sw.B: Wakamjibu, "Mwamini Bwana Yesu, nawe utaokolewa, wewe pamoja na watu wa nyumbani mwako."
sw.R: Wakamwambia, "Mwamini Bwana Yesu. Hapo utaokolewa, na watu wa nyumbani mwako pia."

vi.L: Họ nói: "Hãy tin Chúa Giê-xu, thì ông sẽ được cứu, ông và cả nhà ông."
vi.B: Hai người đáp: "Hãy tin Chúa Giê-xu, thì ông và cả nhà ông sẽ được cứu."
vi.R: Hai người nói: "Hãy tin Chúa Giê-xu. Rồi ông sẽ được cứu, và những người trong nhà ông cũng vậy."

ko.L: 그러자 그들이 말했다. "주 예수를 믿으십시오. 그러면 당신과 당신의 집안이 구원을 받을 것입니다."
ko.B: 그들이 대답했다. "주 예수를 믿으십시오. 그러면 당신과 당신의 집안이 구원을 받을 것입니다."
ko.R: 그들이 말했다. "주 예수를 믿으십시오. 그러면 당신은 구원을 받을 것입니다. 당신 집에 사는 사람들도 구원을 받을 것입니다."

decisions.choice: believe on the Lord Jesus: put your trust in him
decisions.reason: The preposition means on or upon: trust that rests on a person. The same phrase is used in 9:42 and 11:17.

decisions.choice: you and your household: the promise is for them too, as they also believe
alternatives: the household is saved by the jailer's faith alone
decisions.reason: The word is spoken to all in the house (16:32), and the household rejoices together with the jailer, who had believed (16:34). The promise reaches them through the same message and faith; compare 11:14, where Cornelius is told he and his household will be saved.

decisions.choice: the Lord Jesus: Jesus as Lord
decisions.reason: The jailer addressed them as "sirs" (16:30); they point him to the one who is Lord.

decisions.choice: "tu" to the jailer
decisions.reason: The Greek speaks to one man in the singular ("you will be saved, you and your household"), so French says "tu", as in 16:28, following the number of the Greek.

decisions.choice: "tin Chúa Giê-xu" for "believe on the Lord Jesus"
decisions.reason: Put your trust in him (meaning decision); Vietnamese "tin" with a person as object already means trust in him.

source.text: καὶ ἐλάλησαν αὐτῷ τὸν λόγον τοῦ κυρίου σὺν πᾶσι τοῖς ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And they spoke to him the word of the Lord with all the [ones] in the house of him.

en.L: And they spoke the word of the Lord to him, with all those in his house.
en.B: And they shared the word of the Lord with him and with everyone in his household.
en.R: Then Paul and Silas told the Lord's message to him and to everyone in his house.

es.L: Y le hablaron la palabra del Señor, junto con todos los que estaban en su casa.
es.B: Y le comunicaron la palabra del Señor a él y a todos los de su casa.
es.R: Luego Pablo y Silas le contaron el mensaje del Señor a él y a todos los que estaban en su casa.

fr.L: Et ils lui annoncèrent la parole du Seigneur, ainsi qu’à tous ceux qui étaient dans sa maison.
fr.B: Et ils lui firent connaître la parole du Seigneur, à lui et à tous ceux de sa maison.
fr.R: Puis Paul et Silas lui ont annoncé le message du Seigneur, à lui et à tous ceux qui vivaient dans sa maison.

sw.L: Na wakamwambia neno la Bwana, pamoja na wote waliokuwa nyumbani mwake.
sw.B: Kisha wakamweleza neno la Bwana, yeye na wote wa nyumbani mwake.
sw.R: Kisha Paulo na Sila wakamweleza ujumbe wa Bwana yeye na kila mtu aliyekuwa nyumbani mwake.

vi.L: Và họ nói lời của Chúa cho ông cùng với tất cả những người trong nhà ông.
vi.B: Họ giảng lời Chúa cho ông và cho mọi người trong nhà ông.
vi.R: Rồi Phao-lô và Si-la nói sứ điệp của Chúa cho ông và mọi người trong nhà ông nghe.

ko.L: 그리고 그들은 그와 그의 집에 있는 모든 사람에게 주님의 말씀을 전했다.
ko.B: 그리고 그들은 간수와 그 집안의 모든 사람에게 주님의 말씀을 전해 주었다.
ko.R: 그러고 나서 바울과 실라는 간수와 그 집에 있는 모든 사람에게 주님에 관한 말씀을 들려주었다.

decisions.choice: the word of the Lord: the message about the Lord Jesus
decisions.reason: The phrase is used through Acts for the gospel (8:25, 13:44, 15:35).

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "the word of the Lord"
alternatives: some early manuscripts read "the word of God"
decisions.reason: A few early manuscripts have "of God". The sense hardly changes. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the Lord's message
decisions.reason: Readable says what the word was, as at 6:2.

decisions.choice: Paul and Silas
decisions.reason: Readable names the speakers.

source.text: καὶ παραλαβὼν αὐτοὺς ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ὥρᾳ τῆς νυκτὸς ἔλουσεν ἀπὸ τῶν πληγῶν, καὶ ἐβαπτίσθη αὐτὸς καὶ οἱ αὐτοῦ πάντες παραχρῆμα, ἀναγαγών τε αὐτοὺς εἰς τὸν οἶκον παρέθηκεν τράπεζαν καὶ ἠγαλλιάσατο πανοικεὶ πεπιστευκὼς τῷ θεῷ.

records.literal_gloss: And having taken them in that the hour of the night he washed [them] from the wounds, and was baptized he and the [ones] of him all immediately, \v 34 having brought up and them into the house he set before [them] a table, and rejoiced with all the household having believed in the God.

en.L: And taking them in that hour of the night, he washed [them] from their wounds, and he was baptized at once, he and all his [household]; \v 34 and bringing them up into the house, he set a table [before them], and he rejoiced with his whole household, having believed in God.
en.B: Even at that hour of the night he took them and bathed their wounds, and straightaway he was baptized together with all his family. \v 34 Leading them up into his house, he spread a table for them, and the whole household rejoiced with him, now that he had believed in God.
en.R: Even though it was the middle of the night, the jailer took Paul and Silas and washed their wounds. Then he and all his family were baptized right away. \v 34 He took Paul and Silas up into his house and gave them a meal. He and everyone in his house were full of joy, because he now believed in God.

es.L: Y tomándolos en aquella hora de la noche, les lavó las heridas, y fue bautizado él y todos los suyos enseguida; \v 34 y haciéndolos subir a la casa, [les] puso la mesa, y se alegró con toda su casa, por haber creído en Dios.
es.B: Aun a aquella hora de la noche, el carcelero los tomó consigo y les lavó las heridas, y enseguida fue bautizado junto con toda su familia. \v 34 Los llevó a su casa, les preparó la mesa y se llenó de alegría con toda su familia por haber creído en Dios.
es.R: Aunque era plena noche, el carcelero tomó a Pablo y a Silas y les lavó las heridas. Enseguida él y toda su familia fueron bautizados. \v 34 Llevó a Pablo y a Silas a su casa y les dio de comer. Él y todos los de su casa estaban llenos de alegría, porque él ahora creía en Dios.

fr.L: Et les ayant pris avec lui à cette heure même de la nuit, il lava leurs plaies, et il fut baptisé aussitôt, lui et tous les siens ; \v 34 et les ayant fait monter dans sa maison, il [leur] dressa une table, et il se réjouit avec toute sa maisonnée d’avoir cru en Dieu.
fr.B: À cette heure même de la nuit, il les prit avec lui et lava leurs plaies ; puis il fut baptisé sans attendre, avec toute sa famille. \v 34 Il les fit monter chez lui et leur dressa une table, et toute la maisonnée se réjouit avec lui, maintenant qu’il croyait en Dieu.
fr.R: Même si c’était le milieu de la nuit, le gardien a pris Paul et Silas avec lui et il a lavé leurs blessures. Puis lui et toute sa famille ont été baptisés tout de suite. \v 34 Il a fait monter Paul et Silas dans sa maison et leur a donné à manger. Lui et tous ceux de sa maison étaient remplis de joie, parce que maintenant il croyait en Dieu.

sw.L: Na akiwachukua saa ile ya usiku, aliwaosha majeraha yao, na mara moja akabatizwa yeye na watu wake wote; \v 34 na akiwapandisha nyumbani, akawaandalia meza, akafurahi pamoja na nyumba yake yote, akiwa amemwamini Mungu.
sw.B: Hata saa ile ile ya usiku, aliwachukua akawaosha majeraha yao; kisha mara moja yeye na familia yake yote wakabatizwa. \v 34 Aliwapandisha nyumbani kwake, akawaandalia chakula, naye pamoja na familia yake yote akafurahi sana kwa kuwa sasa alikuwa amemwamini Mungu.
sw.R: Ingawa ilikuwa usiku wa manane, mlinzi wa gereza aliwachukua Paulo na Sila, akawaosha majeraha yao. Kisha yeye na familia yake yote wakabatizwa mara moja. \v 34 Akawapeleka Paulo na Sila juu nyumbani kwake, akawapa chakula. Yeye na kila mtu nyumbani mwake walijaa furaha, kwa sababu sasa alikuwa amemwamini Mungu.

vi.L: Và ngay trong giờ ấy của ban đêm, ông đem họ đi rửa các vết thương, và lập tức ông cùng tất cả những người nhà ông đều chịu báp-têm; \v 34 rồi đưa họ lên nhà mình, ông dọn bàn ăn, và vui mừng với cả nhà vì đã tin Đức Chúa Trời.
vi.B: Ngay trong đêm ấy, ông đem hai người đi rửa các vết thương, rồi lập tức ông và cả gia đình đều chịu báp-têm. \v 34 Ông đưa hai người lên nhà mình và dọn bữa ăn cho họ. Cả nhà ông đều vui mừng với ông, vì giờ đây ông đã tin Đức Chúa Trời.
vi.R: Dù lúc ấy đang là nửa đêm, viên cai ngục đem Phao-lô và Si-la đi rửa các vết thương cho họ. Rồi ông và cả gia đình đều chịu báp-têm ngay. \v 34 Ông đưa Phao-lô và Si-la lên nhà mình và dọn bữa ăn cho họ. Ông và mọi người trong nhà đều rất vui mừng, vì bây giờ ông đã tin Đức Chúa Trời.

ko.L: 그리고 그는 그 밤 그 시간에 그들을 데려다가 상처를 씻어 주었고, 그와 그의 모든 [가족이] 곧 세례를 받았다. \v 34 그리고 그들을 자기 집으로 데리고 올라가서 음식상을 차려 주었고, 하나님을 믿게 된 것을 온 집안과 함께 기뻐하였다.
ko.B: 그 밤중에 간수는 그들을 데려다가 상처를 씻어 주었다. 그리고 그와 그의 온 가족이 곧바로 세례를 받았다. \v 34 간수는 그들을 자기 집으로 데리고 올라가서 음식을 대접했다. 그는 하나님을 믿게 되어, 온 집안 식구와 함께 크게 기뻐했다.
ko.R: 한밤중이었지만, 간수는 바울과 실라를 데려다가 그들의 상처를 씻어 주었다. 그리고 그와 그의 온 가족이 바로 세례를 받았다. \v 34 간수는 바울과 실라를 자기 집으로 데리고 올라가서 음식을 대접했다. 간수와 그 집 식구들은 모두 매우 기뻐했다. 이제 그가 하나님을 믿게 되었기 때문이다.

decisions.choice: washed from their wounds, then was baptized: two washings
decisions.reason: He washes the blood from their backs, and then he himself is washed in baptism. The text sets the two acts side by side in the same hour.

decisions.choice: with his whole household: they rejoiced together, and the household also believed
decisions.reason: The word for the whole household may go with "rejoiced" or with "having believed". The participle is singular, about the jailer, but 16:31-33 show the word was spoken to all of them and all were baptized.

decisions.choice: brought them up into the house: the family lived above or beside the prison
decisions.reason: Jailers commonly lived at the prison. "Set a table" means he served them a meal.

decisions.choice: having believed in God: having come to faith in God
alternatives: having always believed in some god
decisions.reason: The perfect tense speaks of a lasting change. For a Gentile, believing in the Lord Jesus (16:31) meant believing in the one God.

decisions.choice: spread a table for them (B); gave them a meal (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture; Readable says what it meant.

decisions.choice: all his family
decisions.reason: The Greek says "all his", meaning his household, as the meaning note on 16:31 explains.

source.text: Ἡμέρας δὲ γενομένης ἀπέστειλαν οἱ στρατηγοὶ τοὺς ῥαβδούχους λέγοντες· Ἀπόλυσον τοὺς ἀνθρώπους ἐκείνους.

records.literal_gloss: Day then having come sent the magistrates the rod-bearers saying, Release the men those.

en.L: And when it was day, the magistrates sent the rod-bearers, saying, "Release those men."
en.B: In the morning the magistrates sent their lictors with the order, "Let those men go."
en.R: The next morning the city officials sent their officers to the jailer with an order: "Let those men go free."

es.L: Y cuando se hizo de día, los magistrados enviaron a los portadores de varas, diciendo: «Suelta a aquellos hombres».
es.B: Por la mañana, los magistrados enviaron a sus lictores con esta orden: «Deja ir a esos hombres».
es.R: A la mañana siguiente, los funcionarios de la ciudad enviaron a sus guardias a decirle al carcelero: «Deja libres a esos hombres».

fr.L: Et quand il fit jour, les magistrats envoyèrent les porteurs de verges, disant : « Relâche ces hommes. »
fr.B: Le matin venu, les magistrats envoyèrent leurs licteurs avec cet ordre : « Laisse partir ces hommes. »
fr.R: Le lendemain matin, les responsables de la ville ont envoyé leurs agents au gardien avec cet ordre : « Libère ces hommes. »

sw.L: Na kulipokucha, mahakimu waliwatuma wabeba-fimbo, wakisema, "Waachilie watu wale."
sw.B: Asubuhi mahakimu waliwatuma askari wao na agizo hili: "Waache watu wale waende."
sw.R: Asubuhi iliyofuata maafisa wa mji waliwatuma askari wao kwa mlinzi wa gereza na agizo hili: "Waache watu wale waende huru."

vi.L: Đến sáng, các quan tòa sai các lính hầu đến nói: "Hãy thả những người ấy."
vi.B: Sáng hôm sau, các quan tòa sai các lính hầu đến truyền lệnh: "Hãy thả những người ấy ra."
vi.R: Sáng hôm sau, các quan chức sai các lính hầu đến báo cho viên cai ngục: "Hãy thả những người ấy ra."

ko.L: 그런데 날이 밝자 행정관들이 막대기를 든 부하들을 보내어 말했다. "그 사람들을 풀어 주어라."
ko.B: 날이 밝자 행정관들이 부하들을 보내어 명령했다. "그 사람들을 풀어 주어라."
ko.R: 다음 날 아침에 도시 관리들이 부하들을 간수에게 보내어 명령했다. "그 사람들을 풀어 주어라."

decisions.choice: the rod-bearers: the lictors, attendants who carried the magistrates' rods
decisions.reason: Roman magistrates were escorted by lictors, who carried bundles of rods as the sign of their power to punish. In a colony the two chief magistrates each had lictors. They had probably carried out the beating of 16:22-23.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: the magistrates simply send the order
alternatives: Codex Bezae adds that the magistrates met in the marketplace and, remembering the earthquake, were afraid
decisions.reason: Codex Bezae and some related witnesses give a reason for the release. The shorter text gives none. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: those men: Paul and Silas
decisions.reason: The order concerns the two who were beaten and jailed the day before.

decisions.choice: lictors
decisions.reason: Balanced uses the Roman title, explained in the meaning note; Literal says what the Greek word means, rod-bearers.

decisions.choice: officers
decisions.reason: Readable uses a plain word for the magistrates' attendants.

decisions.choice: to the jailer
decisions.reason: Readable says to whom the order went, as 16:36 shows.

decisions.choice: los portadores de varas (L); los lictores (B); los guardias (R)
decisions.reason: These were the magistrates' attendants who carried the rods (meaning decision m1). Literal says what the word says, Balanced uses the Roman title as the English does, and Readable names them by their job. The same in verse 38.

decisions.choice: les porteurs de verges (L); les licteurs (B); leurs agents (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: Literal says what the Greek word means, Balanced uses the Roman title, which French also knows as "licteur", and Readable a plain word for the officials' attendants. The order goes to the jailer alone, so it is in the "tu" form.

decisions.choice: wabeba-fimbo (L); askari wao (B, R)
alternatives: a loanword for the Roman lictors
decisions.reason: These were the magistrates' attendants who carried the rods (meaning decision m1). Literal says what the word says; Swahili has no word for a Roman lictor, so Balanced and Readable call them the magistrates' men by their job. The same in verse 38.

decisions.choice: "các lính hầu" for the lictors
decisions.reason: The attendants who carried the magistrates' rods (meaning decision); "lính hầu" is the plain word for officers who serve a magistrate, and the rods have already been named in 16:22.

decisions.choice: "막대기를 든 부하들" (L); "부하들" (B, R) for the lictors, through 16:38; the magistrates give the order in 해라체
decisions.reason: Korean has no word for the Roman lictors; Literal says what their name means, the men who carried the magistrates' rods (meaning decision), and Balanced and Readable say who they were. An order from officials to their men is in the plain style.

source.text: ἀπήγγειλεν δὲ ὁ δεσμοφύλαξ τοὺς λόγους τούτους πρὸς τὸν Παῦλον, ὅτι Ἀπέσταλκαν οἱ στρατηγοὶ ἵνα ἀπολυθῆτε· νῦν οὖν ἐξελθόντες πορεύεσθε ἐν εἰρήνῃ.

records.literal_gloss: Reported then the jailer the words these to the Paul, that, Have sent the magistrates that you may be released; now therefore having come out go in peace.

en.L: And the jailer reported these words to Paul: "The magistrates have sent [word] that you may be released. So now come out [and] go in peace."
en.B: The jailer passed the message on to Paul: "The magistrates have sent orders for your release. So come out now, and go in peace."
en.R: The jailer told Paul, "The city officials have sent word that you can go free. So come out now and go in peace."

es.L: Y el carcelero comunicó estas palabras a Pablo: «Los magistrados han enviado [orden] de que {{plural_you:sean liberados|seáis liberados}}. Ahora, pues, {{plural_you:salgan|salid}} [y] {{plural_you:vayan|id}} en paz».
es.B: El carcelero le pasó el mensaje a Pablo: «Los magistrados han ordenado que {{plural_you:los|os}} pongan en libertad. Así que {{plural_you:salgan|salid}} ya y {{plural_you:vayan|id}} en paz».
es.R: El carcelero le dijo a Pablo: «Los funcionarios de la ciudad mandaron decir que {{plural_you:pueden irse|podéis iros}} libres. Así que {{plural_you:salgan|salid}} ahora y {{plural_you:vayan|id}} en paz».

fr.L: Et le geôlier rapporta ces paroles à Paul : « Les magistrats ont envoyé [dire] qu’on vous relâche. Maintenant donc, sortez [et] allez en paix. »
fr.B: Le geôlier transmit le message à Paul : « Les magistrats ont donné l’ordre de vous libérer. Sortez donc maintenant, et allez en paix. »
fr.R: Le gardien a dit à Paul : « Les responsables de la ville ont fait dire que vous pouvez partir libres. Alors sortez maintenant, et allez en paix. »

sw.L: Na mlinzi wa gereza alimwarifu Paulo maneno haya, kwamba, "Mahakimu wametuma [ujumbe] kwamba mfunguliwe. Basi sasa tokeni mwende kwa amani."
sw.B: Mlinzi wa gereza alimpelekea Paulo ujumbe huo: "Mahakimu wametuma agizo mfunguliwe. Basi tokeni sasa, mwende kwa amani."
sw.R: Mlinzi wa gereza alimwambia Paulo, "Maafisa wa mji wametuma ujumbe kwamba mnaweza kwenda huru. Basi tokeni sasa, mwende kwa amani."

vi.L: Viên cai ngục báo những lời ấy cho Phao-lô: "Các quan tòa đã sai [người đến] để thả các ông; vậy bây giờ hãy ra và đi bình an."
vi.B: Viên cai ngục báo tin cho Phao-lô: "Các quan tòa đã ra lệnh thả các ông. Vậy bây giờ xin các ông ra đi bình an."
vi.R: Viên cai ngục nói với Phao-lô: "Các quan chức đã ra lệnh cho các ông được tự do. Vậy bây giờ các ông hãy ra khỏi đây và đi bình an."

ko.L: 그래서 간수가 이 말을 바울에게 전했다. "행정관들이 여러분을 풀어 주라고 [사람을] 보냈습니다. 그러니 이제 나가셔서 평안히 가십시오."
ko.B: 간수는 이 말을 바울에게 전했다. "행정관들이 여러분을 풀어 주라는 명령을 보냈습니다. 그러니 이제 나가셔서 평안히 가십시오."
ko.R: 간수가 바울에게 말했다. "도시 관리들이 여러분을 풀어 주라는 말을 전해 왔습니다. 이제 나가셔서 평안히 가십시오."

decisions.choice: go in peace: a farewell with a blessing
decisions.reason: The words are a common Jewish farewell (Luke 7:50, 8:48). From the jailer, now a believer, they are a wish for their good.

decisions.choice: you: plural, Paul and Silas
decisions.reason: The jailer speaks to Paul, but the verb is plural.

decisions.choice: the city officials
decisions.reason: Readable uses the plain description chosen at 16:20.

decisions.choice: "các ông" for Paul and Silas in the jailer's mouth
decisions.reason: The jailer, now a believer, keeps the respectful form he used in 16:30.

source.text: ὁ δὲ Παῦλος ἔφη πρὸς αὐτούς· Δείραντες ἡμᾶς δημοσίᾳ ἀκατακρίτους, ἀνθρώπους Ῥωμαίους ὑπάρχοντας, ἔβαλαν εἰς φυλακήν· καὶ νῦν λάθρᾳ ἡμᾶς ἐκβάλλουσιν;

records.literal_gloss: But Paul was saying to them, Having beaten us publicly uncondemned, men Romans being, they threw [us] into prison, and now secretly us they throw out?

en.L: But Paul said to them, "Having beaten us publicly, uncondemned, [though we are] Roman men, they threw [us] into prison, and now are they throwing us out secretly?
en.B: But Paul told them, "We are Roman citizens, and they beat us in front of everyone without condemning us in any court, and threw us into prison. Are they now going to send us away in secret?
en.R: But Paul said to the officers, "We are Roman citizens. The officials beat us in front of everyone, but they never held a trial to show that we had done anything wrong. Then they threw us into prison. Do they now want to send us away secretly?

es.L: Pero Pablo les dijo: «Después de azotarnos públicamente sin condena, siendo [nosotros] hombres romanos, [nos] echaron en la cárcel; ¿y ahora nos echan fuera a escondidas?
es.B: Pero Pablo les respondió: «Somos ciudadanos romanos, y nos azotaron delante de todos sin habernos condenado en ningún juicio, y nos echaron en la cárcel. ¿Y ahora quieren sacarnos de aquí a escondidas?
es.R: Pero Pablo les dijo a los guardias: «Somos ciudadanos romanos. Los funcionarios nos golpearon delante de todos, pero nunca hicieron un juicio para mostrar que habíamos hecho algo malo. Después nos echaron en la cárcel. ¿Y ahora quieren dejarnos ir en secreto?

fr.L: Mais Paul leur dit : « Après nous avoir battus publiquement, sans jugement, nous qui sommes des Romains, ils [nous] ont jetés en prison, et maintenant ils nous font sortir en secret ?
fr.B: Mais Paul leur répondit : « Nous sommes citoyens romains, et ils nous ont fait battre en public sans nous avoir condamnés devant aucun tribunal, puis ils nous ont jetés en prison. Et maintenant, ils voudraient nous renvoyer en secret ?
fr.R: Mais Paul a dit aux agents : « Nous sommes citoyens romains. Les responsables nous ont fait battre devant tout le monde, mais ils n’ont jamais fait de procès pour montrer que nous avions fait quelque chose de mal. Puis ils nous ont jetés en prison. Et maintenant, ils veulent nous faire partir en secret ?

sw.L: Lakini Paulo aliwaambia, "Wakiisha kutupiga hadharani bila kuhukumiwa, sisi tulio watu Warumi, walitutupa gerezani; na sasa wanatutoa kwa siri?
sw.B: Lakini Paulo aliwaambia, "Sisi ni raia wa Rumi, nao wametupiga mbele ya watu wote bila kutuhukumu katika mahakama yoyote, wakatutupa gerezani. Je, sasa wanataka kutufukuza kwa siri?
sw.R: Lakini Paulo aliwaambia wale askari, "Sisi ni raia wa Rumi. Maafisa wa mji walitupiga mbele ya watu wote, lakini hawakufanya kesi kuonyesha kwamba tulikuwa tumefanya kosa lolote. Kisha wakatutupa gerezani. Je, sasa wanataka kutuachilia kwa siri?

vi.L: Nhưng Phao-lô nói với họ: "Họ đã công khai đánh đòn chúng tôi, những người La Mã, khi chưa xét xử, rồi ném vào ngục; và bây giờ họ lại lén đuổi chúng tôi đi sao?
vi.B: Nhưng Phao-lô nói với họ: "Chúng tôi là công dân La Mã, vậy mà họ đã đánh đòn chúng tôi trước mặt mọi người khi chưa hề xét xử, rồi ném chúng tôi vào ngục. Bây giờ họ lại muốn lén đuổi chúng tôi đi sao?
vi.R: Nhưng Phao-lô nói với các lính hầu: "Chúng tôi là công dân La Mã. Các quan chức đã đánh đòn chúng tôi trước mặt mọi người, mà không hề xét xử để chứng minh chúng tôi có làm điều gì sai. Rồi họ ném chúng tôi vào ngục. Bây giờ họ lại muốn lén đuổi chúng tôi đi sao?

ko.L: 그러나 바울이 그들에게 말했다. "그들은 로마 사람인 우리를 재판도 하지 않고 사람들 앞에서 때리고 감옥에 가두었소. 그런데 이제 우리를 몰래 내보내려는 것이오?
ko.B: 그러나 바울이 그들에게 말했다. "우리는 로마 시민이오. 그런데 그들은 재판도 하지 않고 사람들이 보는 앞에서 우리를 때리고 감옥에 가두었소. 그러고는 이제 우리를 몰래 내보내려는 것이오?
ko.R: 그러나 바울이 그 부하들에게 말했다. "우리는 로마 시민이오. 관리들은 우리가 잘못한 것이 있는지 재판도 하지 않고, 모든 사람 앞에서 우리를 때렸소. 그리고 우리를 감옥에 가두었소. 그런데 이제 우리를 몰래 내보내려고 하는 것이오?

decisions.choice: beaten uncondemned, though Romans: a grave breach of Roman law
decisions.reason: Roman law from the Porcian laws onward forbade beating a Roman citizen, and above all without a trial. Cicero's speeches against Verres show how serious it was to treat a citizen so. Paul makes the same claim before a beating in Jerusalem (22:25-29).

decisions.choice: us, Romans: Silas also was a Roman citizen
decisions.reason: Paul speaks in the plural throughout, and the magistrates fear because "they" are Romans (16:38).

decisions.choice: uncondemned: without a trial and verdict
decisions.reason: The word means not condemned by a court. The magistrates had punished them without hearing their case.

decisions.choice: to them: to the lictors, and the jailer
decisions.reason: The lictors carry Paul's words back (16:38), so they were there with the jailer.

decisions.choice: the officers
decisions.reason: Readable names whom Paul spoke to, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: Roman citizens
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what being Roman meant here: citizenship, with its legal rights.

decisions.choice: "người La Mã" (L); "công dân La Mã" (B, R) for "Romans"
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek "men, Romans"; Balanced and Readable say that they were citizens, as the English does.

decisions.choice: Paul answers the magistrates' men in 하오체 ("가두었소", "내보내려는 것이오?")
decisions.reason: Paul protests a wrong done to him and speaks as a Roman citizen to the officials' men: 하오체 is firm without being rude, where 합쇼체 would sound like a plea and 해라체 like an insult. "로마 사람" (L), "로마 시민" (B, R), as the English.

source.text: οὐ γάρ, ἀλλὰ ἐλθόντες αὐτοὶ ἡμᾶς ἐξαγαγέτωσαν.

records.literal_gloss: No indeed, but having come themselves us let them bring out.

en.L: No indeed! But let them come themselves and bring us out."
en.B: Certainly not! Let them come in person and lead us out."
en.R: No! They must come here themselves and walk us out of the prison."

es.L: ¡No, por cierto! Sino que vengan ellos mismos y nos saquen».
es.B: ¡De ninguna manera! Que vengan ellos en persona a sacarnos».
es.R: ¡No! Ellos mismos tienen que venir aquí y sacarnos de la cárcel».

fr.L: Non certes ! Mais qu’ils viennent eux-mêmes nous faire sortir. »
fr.B: Certainement pas ! Qu’ils viennent en personne nous faire sortir. »
fr.R: Non ! Ils doivent venir ici eux-mêmes et nous faire sortir de la prison. »

sw.L: La, hasha! Bali waje wao wenyewe watutoe."
sw.B: Hasha! Waje wao wenyewe watutoe nje."
sw.R: Hapana! Wao wenyewe lazima waje hapa watutoe gerezani."

vi.L: Không đâu, nhưng chính họ hãy đến mà đưa chúng tôi ra."
vi.B: Không được! Chính họ phải đến mà dẫn chúng tôi ra."
vi.R: Không! Chính họ phải đến đây và dẫn chúng tôi ra khỏi ngục."

ko.L: 결코 아니오! 그들이 직접 와서 우리를 데리고 나가게 하시오."
ko.B: 그렇게는 안 되오! 그들이 직접 와서 우리를 데리고 나가야 하오."
ko.R: 그럴 수는 없소! 관리들이 직접 여기 와서 우리를 감옥 밖으로 데리고 나가야 하오."

decisions.choice: let them bring us out: a public sign that they had done nothing wrong
decisions.reason: Luke does not give Paul's reason. Being led out by the magistrates would show the city that the missionaries were innocent, and it may have protected the new believers they left behind (16:40).

decisions.choice: no indeed: a strong refusal
decisions.reason: The two little words together reject the idea outright.

decisions.choice: the quotation opened in 16:37a closes at the end of this sentence
decisions.reason: Both sentences are Paul's words, so French keeps one quotation across the two records, as the English does.

source.text: ἀπήγγειλαν δὲ τοῖς στρατηγοῖς οἱ ῥαβδοῦχοι τὰ ῥήματα ταῦτα· ἐφοβήθησαν δὲ ἀκούσαντες ὅτι Ῥωμαῖοί εἰσιν, καὶ ἐλθόντες παρεκάλεσαν αὐτούς, καὶ ἐξαγαγόντες ἠρώτων ἀπελθεῖν ἀπὸ τῆς πόλεως.

records.literal_gloss: Reported then to the magistrates the rod-bearers the words these; they were afraid then having heard that Romans they are, \v 39 and having come they appealed to them, and having brought [them] out they were asking [them] to go away from the city.

en.L: And the rod-bearers reported these words to the magistrates, and they were afraid when they heard that they were Romans, \v 39 and they came and appealed to them, and bringing [them] out, they asked [them] to go away from the city.
en.B: The lictors carried these words back to the magistrates, who were frightened to hear that the men were Roman citizens. \v 39 They came and pleaded with them, and after leading them out, they kept asking them to leave the city.
en.R: The officers told the city officials what Paul had said. The officials were afraid when they heard that Paul and Silas were Roman citizens. \v 39 So they came and said they were sorry. They led them out of the prison and asked them to leave the city.

es.L: Y los portadores de varas comunicaron estas palabras a los magistrados; y tuvieron miedo al oír que eran romanos, \v 39 y viniendo, les rogaron, y sacándolos, [les] pedían que se fueran de la ciudad.
es.B: Los lictores llevaron estas palabras a los magistrados, que se asustaron al oír que aquellos hombres eran ciudadanos romanos. \v 39 Vinieron a hablarles con buenas palabras, y después de sacarlos, les pedían una y otra vez que se fueran de la ciudad.
es.R: Los guardias les contaron a los funcionarios de la ciudad lo que Pablo había dicho. Los funcionarios tuvieron miedo cuando oyeron que Pablo y Silas eran ciudadanos romanos. \v 39 Así que vinieron y les pidieron disculpas. Los sacaron de la cárcel y les pidieron que se fueran de la ciudad.

fr.L: Et les porteurs de verges rapportèrent ces paroles aux magistrats ; et ceux-ci eurent peur en apprenant qu’ils étaient Romains, \v 39 et ils vinrent les apaiser, et les ayant fait sortir, ils [leur] demandaient de quitter la ville.
fr.B: Les licteurs rapportèrent ces paroles aux magistrats, qui prirent peur en apprenant que ces hommes étaient citoyens romains. \v 39 Ils vinrent leur parler avec ménagement, les firent sortir et les prièrent avec insistance de quitter la ville.
fr.R: Les agents ont raconté aux responsables de la ville ce que Paul avait dit.
